description: The three lanes an API walk judges apart, each on its own evidence: contract, that every case the runner named held; data, that every record the run wrote lies inside the seed's namespace and none outside it, read back through the API; lifecycle, that the namespace was verified read-only and then deleted, and nothing else was. There is no fourth lane and no lane may be omitted. The record also carries where the run was appended, so a reader finds the history without opening the flow folder first.

flowRoot.description: The flow directory on this machine, so the appended record can be read back where it was written.

resultRef.description: The run record this result was appended as. The API history of a flow lives beside the browser history and never inside it.

latestRef.description: The pointer file that names the newest API run. It is a file holding a run id, never a symlink.

historyRef.description: The one-line-per-run history of this flow's API walks, appended to and never rewritten.

records.description: Every record this run's suite created, read back through the API as a client reads it, with whether it lies inside the run namespace. A record outside it is a leak: the suite wrote where the flow does not own the rows, and no cleanup this operator may perform can take it back.

readBackRef.description: The API read that proved the record stands: the route the client called and where its answer is recorded. A record proved by a direct store query is not proved as a client sees it.

cleanup.description: Cleanup deletes the run namespace and nothing else; a run record is history and is never deleted.

verifiedReadOnly.description: Verification read and did not write. A verification that wrote is a second run of the suite wearing a checker's clothes.
